metaDescription: Six swivel vegetable peelers compared on blade flex, handle build and cleanup, from the OXO classics to Farberware, Deiss and Gorilla Grip.
introParagraphs: A swivel peeler, sometimes called a Euro or floating-blade peeler, mounts its blade on a small pivot so it rocks along the surface of whatever you are peeling. That one design choice is why it handles lumpy potatoes, round apples and slim carrots with fewer awkward wrist turns than a fixed blade. All six picks here use that idea, and the differences come down to handle build, weight, extras and warranty.

We evaluated each pick from the specifications and features on its product page, comparing handle shape, materials, safety extras and cleanup claims. WorthRated is written for active adults who cook often and for the family members who buy kitchen tools for them. Nothing here has been put through hands-on lab measurement.

The short version: the OXO Good Grips Swivel Peeler is the all-around choice, the OXO Good Grips Pro is the sturdiest, the Gorilla Grip has the longest handle, and the Deiss PRO carries a lifetime warranty. Farberware and Spring Chef fill the simpler, lighter slots.

products.name: OXO Good Grips Swivel Peeler
products.description:
This OXO model is the swivel peeler most other brands copy. Two flexible blades pivot independently of the handle, which lets them hug potatoes, apples and other tough-skinned produce without much steering from you. The soft oversized handle is designed for long, repetitive jobs.

What sets it apart in a crowded field is how the thick grip lets you relax your hand, since you need less squeeze to hold it steady. The listing says the grip stays firm even when your hands are wet. If you have small hands, the bulk may feel more than you need, and a swivel head is less efficient on very large squash than a wide fixed blade.

A built-in eye remover handles potato blemishes, and a large hole in the handle lets you store it on a hook. Next to the OXO Good Grips Pro, it is the softer, lighter-feeling option, while the Pro uses a die-cast zinc body for a heavier feel. Against Farberware, it offers a more cushioned handle and a more established design. Because it is so widely copied, it is also easy to find replacement peelers in the same style if you ever need one.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want the classic soft-handled swivel peeler for everyday jobs.
pros: Floating twin blades hug curved produce
Thick soft handle relaxes the hand
Grip holds firm when wet
Eye remover and hang hole included
cons: Less efficient on very large squash

products.name: OXO Good Grips Pro Swivel Peeler
products.description:
The Pro version swaps the all-rubber feel of the standard OXO for a die-cast zinc body and an extra-hardened stainless steel blade that the maker says stays sharp. The contoured handle carries extra cushioning to keep the grip ergonomic. It also includes a sharp eyer for removing blemishes.

The metal body makes it feel planted, so it suits cooks who press a little harder or peel in volume. That heft is also its downside: it is heavier than the plastic swivel peelers, and a small or tired hand may notice the difference after a long session. The listing is short, so details such as dimensions or a hang hole are not given.

Cleanup is straightforward since it is dishwasher safe. Compared with the OXO Good Grips Swivel Peeler, it gives up the oversized soft profile for a firmer, more structured build. Against the Gorilla Grip, it is a more compact tool with a harder body rather than a long, rubber-wrapped handle. It suits cooks who like to press firmly on stubborn skins like thick potato or beet peel.
products.bestFor: Frequent cooks who prefer a solid metal-bodied swivel peeler.
pros: Die-cast zinc body feels solid and durable
Extra-hardened stainless blade holds its edge
Cushioned contoured handle for comfort
Dishwasher safe
cons: No hang hole or guard listed

products.name: Deiss PRO Swivel Vegetable Peeler
products.description:
The Deiss PRO uses smooth dual blades on a precision swivel head that the maker says glides around bumps and grooves. It aims for a thin, even peel that saves produce, and the listing says it does not clog or corrode with consistent use. The handle is soft-touch rubber with a non-slip grip.

A detail worth noting is the construction: the listing says no water gets trapped in the handle, which avoids the musty, heavy handle problem some hollow peelers develop. The grip is a regular size rather than oversized, so it sits between the Farberware and OXO in padding. The arthritis mention in the listing is a marketing claim, so treat comfort as something to try for yourself.

It is dishwasher safe and backed by a lifetime warranty, the strongest support promise in this swivel lineup. Compared with the Spring Chef Original, it is a similar rubber-gripped swivel with a clearer warranty. Next to the OXO Good Grips Pro, it is lighter but less rugged.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a rubber-gripped swivel with a lifetime warranty.
pros: Lifetime warranty from the maker
Soft-touch non-slip rubber grip
No water trapped in the handle
Thin even peel saves produce
cons: Standard-size handle, less padded than OXO
No guard or hang hole listed

products.name: GORILLA GRIP Patented Vegetable and Potato Peeler
products.description:
The Gorilla Grip has dual swiveling stainless steel blades that cut in both directions, mounted on an oversized handle that measures nearly 8 inches. The handle is soft-touch rubber with a patented slip resistant shape. The maker also says it is BPA-free and third-party tested as food grade.

The longer handle gives you room to choke up for control or hold back for leverage, which suits larger hands. It also means the peeler takes more drawer room than the compact swivels, and a long body gives slightly less fine control on tiny produce. It is rust resistant and dishwasher safe.

A plastic guard comes with it, which the compact OXO and Farberware designs lack. A built-in potato eyer is also included. Compared with the Spring Chef Original, it is longer and more guarded but heavier in the hand. Against the Deiss PRO, it offers more handle in place of a lifetime warranty.
products.bestFor: Cooks with larger hands who want a long handle and a blade guard.
pros: Nearly 8 inch handle suits larger hands
Blade guard protects edge in storage
Dual blades cut in both directions
Rust resistant and dishwasher safe
cons: Long body takes more drawer room

products.name: Farberware Euro Vegetable Peeler with Swivel Blade
products.description:
The Farberware Euro peeler has a razor-sharp stainless steel swivel blade that follows the natural contour of produce. The listing says it handles apples, peaches, zucchini, eggplant and potatoes, and that it also shaves hard cheeses and chocolate. The oversized ergonomic grip is meant to cut hand fatigue on long jobs.

The breadth of use is what makes it stand out, since the same tool can finish a dessert garnish. The listing describes it as compact enough to fit drawers or cabinets, while the built-in hang hole supports hooks, pantries and pegboards. It does not mention a potato eyer, so potato blemishes need a knife tip.

The blade is rust resistant and dishwasher safe. Compared with the OXO Good Grips Swivel Peeler, it adds garnish versatility but drops the stated eye remover. Next to the Spring Chef Original, it offers an oversized grip instead of a light, rubber-gripped body. The garnish ability makes it a good gift for someone who bakes and cooks in equal measure.
products.bestFor: Cooks who also want to shave cheese or chocolate with the same tool.
pros: Razor-sharp stainless swivel blade
Oversized ergonomic grip for long jobs
Also shaves hard cheese and chocolate
Hang hole and compact enough for drawers

products.name: Spring Chef Original Swivel Vegetable Peeler
products.description:
The Spring Chef Original is a plain, light swivel peeler with dual stainless steel blades that the maker says stay ultra sharp. A non-slip rubber handle works for both right and left hands, and a built-in blemish remover is included. The listing says it does not clog with peels.

Its selling points are low weight and simplicity. The listing calls it lightweight and easy to use, even for those with arthritis, which hints at a design aimed at comfort over heft. The handle is slimmer than the OXO's oversized grip, so people who want a big cushion should look elsewhere.

It has a hang hole and is dishwasher safe. Compared with the Deiss PRO, it has a similar rubber-gripped swivel layout but no stated warranty. Next to the OXO Good Grips Pro, it is far lighter and has a looser, less rugged feel. It works well as a spare for a second kitchen. It is a straightforward spare to keep near the sink or take to a holiday house.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want a light, no-fuss swivel peeler with a rubber grip.
pros: Lightweight and easy to maneuver
Rubber handle works in either hand
Blemish remover and hang hole included
Dishwasher safe and resists clogging
cons: Slimmer handle than the oversized OXO

buyingCriteria.explanation: The point of a swivel peeler is a blade that rocks to follow the produce. Look for twin or dual blades that cut in both directions so you do not lift between strokes. The Gorilla Grip and OXO Good Grips Swivel Peeler both use dual swiveling blades. A stiff, fixed head defeats the purpose and forces more wrist turn. Test the swivel by rolling the blade against a flat surface and noting how freely it tilts without wobbling sideways.

Handle shape controls fatigue more than the blade does. A thick, soft grip spreads pressure while a slim hard one concentrates it. The OXO Good Grips Swivel Peeler and Farberware use oversized grips, while the Spring Chef Original is slimmer and lighter. Pick the profile that fits your hand. A handle with a hanging hole or a wider base also gives your thumb a natural resting point during long pulls.

Heavy metal bodies feel planted, and light plastic bodies feel nimble. The OXO Good Grips Pro uses a die-cast zinc body, while the Spring Chef Original is described as lightweight. For short jobs, weight rarely matters, but a big batch of potatoes shows the difference quickly. Choose based on how long you typically peel. Weight also affects how well the peeler rests on a counter edge, so think about where it will live between uses.

A built-in eyer saves reaching for a knife on potatoes. The OXO Good Grips Swivel Peeler and Gorilla Grip include one, while the Farberware listing does not. Extras like guards or hang holes also count, since they protect blades in storage. Decide which extras you will actually use. A blemish tool is also useful for sprouting spots on older potatoes, so it earns its place beyond looks.

Stainless steel blades resist rust and the dishwasher. The Deiss PRO says it does not corrode and traps no water in the handle, and the Gorilla Grip is rust resistant. A peeler that clogs with peel is annoying to clear. Look for open blade spacing and dishwasher-safe claims.

Swivel blades dull with use, so plan to replace the peeler eventually regardless of coverage. The Deiss PRO lists a lifetime warranty, which is the clearest support in this guide. Other picks list none. Treat warranty as a tie-breaker, not a reason to skip sharpness. Check the claim details on the product page, since lifetime terms vary between makers.

howWeEvaluated.title: Swivel action
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared how each listing describes its blade pivot and whether the blades cut in both directions. The Gorilla Grip and OXO Good Grips Swivel Peeler describe dual or twin swiveling blades, and the Deiss PRO describes a precision swivel head. Clear descriptions earned more credit. A swivel that wobbles sideways or sticks would lose points, but we can only judge from what each listing says about its mechanism.

howWeEvaluated.title: Handle comfort
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed size, material and padding. The OXO Good Grips Swivel Peeler and Farberware lead with oversized grips, the Gorilla Grip leads on length at nearly 8 inches, and the Spring Chef Original leads on lightness.

howWeEvaluated.title: Build quality
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at body and blade materials. The OXO Good Grips Pro stands out with die-cast zinc and an extra-hardened blade, while the others rely on plastic or rubber handles with stainless blades.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety and storage
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked guards, hang holes and compact size. The Gorilla Grip includes a guard, and the OXO Good Grips Swivel Peeler, Farberware and Spring Chef Original include hang holes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Support and value
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered warranty and extras. The Deiss PRO lists a lifetime warranty and the Farberware adds cheese and chocolate shaving. We relied on product specs and buyer feedback, not hands-on measurement. Scores are editorial and reflect fit for everyday home cooks, not laboratory results.

faq.q: What does swivel mean on a peeler?
faq.a: It means the blade is mounted on a small pivot so it rocks to follow the shape of the produce. This reduces wrist turning on curved items like apples and potatoes. All six picks use a swivel head. It is different from a fixed Y blade. If a peeler feels like it chatters on the skin, check that the pivot moves freely.

faq.q: Is a swivel peeler better than a Y-peeler?
faq.a: Neither is better outright. Swivel peelers handle curves and bumps, while Y-peelers move fast on large, even produce. Many cooks keep one of each. If you want only one, the OXO Good Grips Swivel Peeler covers the widest range.

Weight gives a stable feel but adds fatigue over long jobs. The OXO Good Grips Pro is the heavy-bodied pick, and the Spring Chef Original is the light one. Choose based on how long you peel at a time. Try to hold both styles in a store if you can, since feel varies by hand.

Some do if the blade spacing is tight. Deiss PRO and Spring Chef Original both say they do not clog with peels. Clearing peel with a quick rinse is usually enough. Wet starchy peel is the most likely to jam any design.

faq.q: Can I put a swivel peeler in the dishwasher?
faq.a: Most listings here say dishwasher safe, including the OXO Good Grips Pro, Deiss PRO, Gorilla Grip, Farberware and Spring Chef Original. Check the product page for your exact model since user reports sometimes differ. Hand washing and drying extends blade life. Rinse promptly after peeling starchy vegetables so residue does not dry on the blade.

faq.q: How long does a swivel blade stay sharp?
faq.a: It depends on use and the steel, but most cooks eventually notice dragging or extra passes. That is the sign to replace it. Many cooks swap peelers about once a year, and low-cost options make this easy.

faq.q: Can I use these to shave cheese or chocolate?
faq.a: The Farberware listing explicitly says it excels at shaving hard cheeses and chocolate. Other swivel peelers can often do similar jobs, but only that listing says so. Use a clean, dry blade and firm items for best results. Always wipe the blade dry afterward to protect the edge.
